name: 360 Orbit NoCookie Analytics
author: Jörg Liwa

sections.description:
NoCookie Analytics shows you the key figures of your website without collecting personal data about your visitors:

  • No cookies, no raw IP storage. Visitors are recognized by a pseudonymous hash (SHA-256 of IP + user agent + secret salt). The salt changes daily, so a visitor can only be recognized within a single day.
  • Bots and logged-in editors are automatically excluded from the count.
  • Clear dashboard with a time series chart (visitors/page views) and the most visited pages.
  • Configurable automatic deletion of old data.

Free vs. Pro

The free version includes full tracking, the dashboard with week, month, 6-month, year and custom date ranges, and the configurable retention period (default around 13 months, 0 = never delete).

NoCookie Analytics Pro adds:

  • CSV export of the time series.
  • Visitor details: browsers, operating systems, devices, screen sizes (in coarse steps), referrers (host name only) and languages.
  • Export and import of the settings as JSON.
  • Automatic update notifications directly in the WordPress admin.

Third-party libraries

  • Chart.js 4.6.1 (MIT license) draws the time series chart in the dashboard. It is included as the unmodified minified file assets/chart.umd.min.js (build dist/chart.umd.js from the npm package chart.js). Source code: https://github.com/chartjs/Chart.js/tree/v4.6.1
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin ZIP under Plugins → Add New → Upload Plugin.
  2. Activate the plugin. Tracking then runs automatically.
  3. View your statistics in the Statistics menu.
sections.faq:
Do I need a cookie consent banner for this plugin?

The plugin sets no cookies and stores no raw IP addresses. Visitors are recognized exclusively by a pseudonymous, non-reversible hash. Whether consent is still legally required depends on your overall setup and the applicable law; this does not replace individual legal advice.

Where is the data stored?

Exclusively in a dedicated table in your WordPress database. No external servers, no third parties.

Can I reset the salt?

Yes, under Settings. This invalidates all previous visitor hashes (useful after a security incident, for example).

Liability in case of damage?

This plugin is provided without any warranty (“as is”). The developer accepts no liability for data loss or damage resulting from the use of the plugin. Creating a complete backup before use is strongly recommended.
sections.changelog:
1.1.3

  • New: a “Visitors” box on the 360 WP Orbit overview, optionally also on the WordPress dashboard.

1.1.2

  • Changed: the 360 WP Orbit overview shows the important boxes of the active plugins at the top, optionally also on the WordPress dashboard; all boxes and tables now use one width.

1.1.1

  • Maintenance release for the free version; the Pro version gains a setup assistant.

1.1.0

  • New: live view on the Statistics tab (visitors of the last 5 minutes, views and visitors today, pages being viewed, team online). Updates every 30 seconds.
  • New: setting to also count visits of logged-in editors and administrators (off by default).
  • Changed: buttons, the License tab and Export/Import now look the same in all plugins of the suite (primary actions in the plugin colour, cards side by side).

1.0.28

  • New: the texts of the plugin appear in German by default, also on sites in another language; under 360 WP Orbit > Overview the language can be switched to the language of the website. The WordPress.org package follows the language of the website and now ships the German translation itself, so no language pack is needed.

1.0.27

  • Changed: content boxes are 960 px wide as in the other 360 Orbit plugins and the License tab.

1.0.26

  • Changed: the Settings tab follows the layout of the WordPress settings screens. The retention period is a “Keep data for” row with a days field, the explanation and the number of stored hits below it.
  • Changed: resetting the visitor salt now sits in a separate, red-outlined danger zone at the end of the Settings tab and still asks for confirmation.
  • Changed: on the Statistics tab, the range buttons and the From/To date filter share one toolbar. More space above the chart, and an empty period shows “No visits recorded in this period yet.” instead of a blank chart.
  • Changed: in Pro, the CSV export notice spans the full width, and the license tab uses the same layout; disconnecting has its own danger zone.
